subject: System Design
title: TLS: Encrypting the Web
description: A micro-lesson that makes TLS: Encrypting the Web usable.

hook.text: Without TLS, anyone on your Wi-Fi can read your passwords, emails, and credit card numbers in plain text.

buildup.text: TLS encrypts the connection between your browser and the server so eavesdroppers see only gibberish.

discovery.text: TLS 1.3 reduced the handshake to one round trip, making encrypted connections nearly as fast as unencrypted.

twist.text: TLS encrypts data in transit but not at rest. Your data is decrypted on the server and could be exposed there.

climax.text: Over 95% of web traffic is now encrypted with TLS. The unencrypted web is effectively dead.

punchline.text: TLS makes eavesdropping on web traffic impossible.

quiz.question: What does TLS protect?
options: Data in transit between client and server
